description: Compare ci-observe captures that ran the same thing. Pick a cohort from the tables at the top: exact cohorts (keyed on the resolved osac commit, harness checkout SHA, workflow SHA and exact pytest selection; empty until the Q1 identity fields reach live captures) or source-revision cohorts (requested osac commit and suite word, excluding captures with resolved harness SHAs; not exact). The comparison tables then rank tests by observed test-span time and list what failed. Observed time is test-span time; it is not runner time.

panels.title: Pick a cohort
panels.description: What a cohort is, the sample rule, and what this page can and cannot tell you.

options.content:
Exact cohorts require resolved source and harness SHAs; they appear once the Q1 identity fields reach live captures. Source-only cohorts are grouped by osac commit and suite word; they are **not exact** and are **not a baseline**, because the harness revision was not captured for them.

**The sample rule:** a comparison needs at least 2 captures in the cohort, and a stable median needs 3. The **Sample status** line under the cohort tables states where the current selection stands. When it says "No baseline", the tables below show a single run's tests, not a comparison.

**Observed time is not runner time.** Test spans include each test's setup and call time, tests run in parallel and overlap, and the total cannot be converted into runner minutes.

**Loading:** panels can take up to two minutes to load; a blank body while loading is not an empty result. Each panel runs one TraceQL search against a slow trace backend, and a loaded panel states its own result: a number, a verdict, or an explicit empty message.

Failed-test evidence is collapsed at the bottom of the page; expand that row to inspect it. Click the OSAC commit value in a cohort row to load that cohort. You pick the cohort here. The run detail page links to this page but does not preselect a capture.

panels.title: How to read this comparison
panels.description: Cohort kinds and how to read the tables.

options.content:
### Two kinds of cohort
**Exact cohorts** compare captures that share the full resolved run identity: the resolved osac commit (`osac.ci.test_sha`), the resolved harness checkout SHA, the reusable workflow file SHA, and the exact pytest suite, filter and marker. The requested osac ref is shown as metadata only; a moving ref never keys a cohort. Exact cohorts appear once the Q1 identity fields reach live captures; until then the exact table stays empty. Only cohorts with at least 2 captures are listed.

**Source-revision cohorts (not exact)** group captures by requested osac commit (a pinned SHA) and suite word. Captures whose harness checkout or workflow SHA resolved to a real commit are excluded, so exact and source rows never mix. The harness revision was not captured for the remaining runs, so this is not an exact comparison and must not be used as a regression baseline.

The table you click decides the mode: an exact cohort sets the resolved-SHA variables, a source cohort sets the osac commit and suite word and clears the resolved SHAs. The exact filters match only when every resolved-SHA variable holds a full SHA.

### Reading the tables
- **Tests using the most time** ranks tests by total observed test-span time in the selected cohort; its Captures column is the number of run attempts included (capture IDs carry the attempt). The Test column shows the test function; the Full test id column carries the complete pytest node id.
- **Failed tests in this cohort** lists the tests whose spans report error, with the captures they failed in. Compare it with the table above: a test high in both lists is where time and failures coincide. This is evidence, not a diagnosis: duration does not explain a failure.
- **Failed runs in this cohort** lists each failed test occurrence, with a link from the capture ID to the run investigation page.
- **Runs in this cohort** lists the captures behind every table above, from the cohort's own test spans. Session status and run duration are not joined here; the capture link opens the run investigation page, which has them.
- The sample status above the tables states the cohort size and its verdict. The failed-test tables sit in a collapsed row: empty means none were recorded, not broken.
- `all` and `none` are literal selection values, not wildcards.
- A test's rows are keyed by its pytest node id, and duplicate spans for one test in one capture are summed first, so a rerun cannot inflate the capture count.

panels.title: Query limits (verified against this backend on 2026-11-01)
panels.description: The caps this dashboard's queries actually hit, with the numbers observed live.

options.content:
- The query limit is 30,000 spansets (traces), not spans: one single-capture query returned exactly 30,000 traces holding 38,902 spans.
- Each query returns at most 100 spans per spanset; the backend rejects higher values (`spans per span set exceeds 100`). All of a capture's pytest spans sit in one trace, so a query matching more than 100 spans in a capture loses the rest: a 47-test capture returned all 47 parent test spans but only 100 of its ~190 total test spans. Parent-test-span queries are complete while a capture holds at most 100 parent tests (the most observed is 53).
- The backend rejects time ranges longer than 168 hours (7 days). Keep the dashboard time range at or below that.
- A live capture is not final: its spans arrive while the run is in progress, and freshly flushed blocks are invisible to search for up to 15 minutes.
- Captures without the Q1 identity fields are excluded from exact cohorts.
- Source-revision cohorts exclude resolved harness SHAs with structural negation (`!( attribute =~ sha )`), which this Tempo evaluates correctly: it kept all 5,382 test spans when the attribute was absent and dropped exactly the 26 spans whose osac ref is a resolved SHA. Matching absent attributes with `= nil` is not usable here: standalone it does match absent attributes, but combined with span predicates it returned nothing, and combined with other attribute predicates it overshot the backend's 16 MB response limit.
- Every panel runs exactly one TraceQL query by design: this Grafana's Tempo plugin executes only the first query of a panel and overwrites every additional target with it (verified 2026-11-02 from the served plugin bundle and captured browser requests), so a multi-target panel would silently run its first query repeatedly.
- Panel load time is the backend, not the page: a single query took 5 to 20 seconds when measured alone on 2026-11-02, and this page runs ten of them. Under that concurrent load the backend intermittently fails: Tempo's search returns `429 job queue full`, which Grafana surfaces as `Get "http://…/api/search": …` on the panel (both observed live on 2026-11-02). A failed panel shows a red error badge and its empty-state text; refreshing retries.
